Wife’s convenience alone can’t decide where matrimonial case is heard, Allahabad High Court

The Allahabad High Court has refused to transfer a husband’s restitution of conjugal rights case from Aligarh to Gautam Budh Nagar, holding that the wife’s convenience, the child’s schooling and the pendency of a maintenance case elsewhere do not automatically justify transfer.

The wife argued that she was living in Gautam Budh Nagar with the minor child and that travelling to Aligarh would cause financial hardship and disrupt the child’s education. She also pointed out that her maintenance case was already pending in Gautam Budh Nagar.

The High Court held that while these are relevant factors, the decisive test is whether refusing transfer would cause genuine hardship or a failure of justice. Section 24 CPC, it said, cannot be used merely to secure a more convenient forum.

The Court also noted that the wife had not shown that attending proceedings in Aligarh was impracticable or that she would be denied a fair opportunity to defend the case. The existence of a separate maintenance proceeding in Gautam Budh Nagar was also held insufficient by itself to justify transfer.

Finding no exceptional circumstances, the High Court dismissed the transfer plea and directed the Family Court at Aligarh to proceed with the husband’s restitution petition expeditiously.
